This document 
outlines the inspection checklist I2, which 
must be carried out on a monthly 
bases as indicated in the above 
title block by M1. The 
first draft has been 
initiated by eng. El-Sayed 
Abdel Moneam El-Geddawy and 
tested at 06 May 2002 for battery no.1 at Sheraton El Matar 66kv Substation, 
Cairo zone.
A work permit must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category,

items: A work permit must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category,
No smoking in battery room or any things leads to fire

Using safety equipments, and isolated tools, safety goggles, rubber gloves, rubber apron 
and safety boots is necessary

Do not put any tools or metal things on the top of battery (to avoid short 
circuit danger)
Do not use the same tools for maintenance in alkaline cells and acidic ells

Repeat the inspection that must 
 be made according to MPIS document no. B-016-r0

Disconnect the AC supply of the 
 battery charger

Record the whole voltage of the 
 battery

Inspect all cells from outside to 
 discover if there is leakage of electrolyte, cracks in electrolyte container 
 *body of cell)

Record the density of each cell 
 and check if the density is in the save values (the save range is between 
 1.16, 1.12 gm / cm3), write the values in the maintenance card

If you find any cell has low or 
 over density values (under 1.19 or above 1.12 gm / cm3), use electrolyte or 
 distilled water to get the save value and record what you did
 - Cell no : 
 - The density : 
 - Treated or not :

If you discover defective cells 
 you must replace it with a new one (according recommended procedures to save 
 people and equipments)

Inspect the electrolyte level (10 
 - 15 mm above the highest of electrodes according to manufacturer), use 
 distilled water to get the correct level and record that in battery battery 
 sheets as: 
 - Cell no. (that has low level): 
 - Treated or not

Inspect the connectors and 
 terminals of cells and remove any deposits of salt (if exists)

Check and tighten well the 
 connectors between cells
Clean tops of cells

Lubricate cells terminals with a 
 thin film of Vaseline

Avoid coating the rubber parts 
 with Vaseline, because Vaseline damages it.

Read the voltage of every cell 
 and record it in maintenance card (standard value is 1.3 v / cell

Record the whole voltage of the 
 battery, and compare it with the reading taken in step 3, write the readings 
 in the maintenance card

If the new reading of battery 
 voltage is below 215V, you must put the battery under high charging position 
 for about 6 hours, and then put the battery under normal charge.

Record (again) the battery 
 voltage after the high charging and compare it with the previous readings
